subject.title: fix(runtime): cancelled workflows no longer continue external commands

question: When cancellation arrives during an already-started side-effecting command, should Lobster preserve the completed result while halting the remaining pipeline, and which envelope status should represent that partial success?
rationale: The current contract can return normal output, which continues the pipeline, or throw or halt in ways that may discard or misclassify a definitive completed send; the durable partial-result contract needs runtime-owner intent.

options.title: Add partial-success cancellation
options.body: Preserve completed send results, halt all later stages, and expose an explicit cancellation or partial-result envelope with focused regression coverage.

options.title: Return cancellation error
options.body: Throw after the in-flight send settles so later stages stop, accepting that completed result data may only appear in error details or logs.

options.title: Allow downstream continuation
options.body: Keep normal output semantics after the completed send and narrow the PR claim to stopping only later drafts and owned subprocesses.

recommendation.title: Add partial-success cancellation
recommendation.body: Preserve completed send results, halt all later stages, and expose an explicit cancellation or partial-result envelope with focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties steipete most directly to the runtime continuation and tool-envelope contract that must represent partial success under cancellation.
